title: Alliance Reports Third Quarter 2025 Results
summary: Revenue increased 14% vs. prior year with strong performance across all end markets …...
body_text: Revenue increased 14% vs. prior year with strong performance across all end markets Net Income of $32.9 million reflecting robust topline, cost optimization and manufacturing leverage Adjusted EBITDA increased 16% vs. prior year from high demand and operational execution Advanced innovation leadership with launch of industry's largest stack tumbler and new payment technology solution for the Vended market Strengthened balance sheet with repayment of debt with IPO proceeds in October 2025 RIPON, Wis. , Nov. 13, 2025 /PRNewswire/ -- Alliance Laundry Systems (NYSE: ALH) ("Alliance" or the "Company"), the global leader in commercial laundry equipment, announced results today for its third quarter ended September 30, 2025. "Alliance delivered strong performance in our first reported quarter as a public company with double-digit growth on both the top and bottom line, and disciplined execution on our strategic initiatives," said Michael Schoeb, CEO of Alliance Laundry. "Using proceeds from our successful IPO in October, we meaningfully reduced leverage while investing in our key long-term growth opportunities. Our balanced capital allocation strategy and relentless focus on quality and reliability enhance our position as the leading, pure-play commercial laundry systems manufacturer." THIRD QUARTER 2025 CONSOLIDATED RESULTS Net revenues were $437.6 million, an increase of 14% compared to $384.3 million in the prior year quarter. The increase was driven by both strong volume performance and low to mid-single digit price increases. The strong performance across both North America and International reportable segments was due to continued robust demand across the Vended, On-Premise Laundry (OPL), and Commercial-In-Home (CIH) end markets. The high demand reflects the attractive total cost of ownership offering Alliance provides that addresses continued customer needs for durable and reliable commercial laundry solutions. Net income was $32.9 million, an increase of 620% compared to net loss of $(6.3) million in the prior year quarter. Net income improvement in the quarter was driven by strong operating performance, lower interest expense, and refinancing expenses in the prior year quarter. Adjusted net income was $48.4 million, a 47% increase versus the prior year period. Net income margin expanded year-over-year to 8%, an increase of 920 basis points. Adjusted EBITDA was $110.8 million, an increase of 16% compared to $95.9 million in the prior year quarter. The increase reflects strong revenue growth, disciplined operating expense management and continued strategic investments in product innovation, and commercial and corporate functions to support long-term growth and public company infrastructure. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded year-over-year to 25%, an increase of 40 basis points. THIRD QUARTER 2025 RESULTS BY REPORTABLE SEGMENT North America revenue was $330.7 million, an increase of 14%, compared to $289.2 million in the prior year quarter with strong double digit growth across all three end markets, driven by a combination of mid-single digit price increases, and low double digit increases in volume. North America Adjusted EBITDA was $95.4 million, an increase of 13%, compared to $84.2 million for the prior year quarter. Performance was driven by gross margin expansion including manufacturing efficiencies, offset by strategic investments to support future value creation initiatives. Tariff impact in the quarter was $3.5 million and was largely offset by price increases. International revenue was $106.9 million, an increase of 12%, compared to $95.1 million for the prior year quarter. Growth was balanced across mature and developing markets, with approximately one-third of the increase attributable to each of volume, price, and favorable foreign exchange. International Adjusted EBITDA was $25.7 million, an increase of 9%, compared to $23.4 million for the prior year quarter with strong topline performance partially offset by customer and product mix. The Company's local-for-local manufacturing strategy resulted in limited tariff exposure in the quarter. THIRD QUARTER 2025 BUSINESS HIGHLIGHTS Strengthened capital structure with repricing of Term Loan B facility resulting in a 25 basis point interest rate reduction, and a voluntary $135.0 million debt paydown, positioning the Company for future interest savings. Showcased leading innovation at Clean Show 2025 with product and technology launches including: Industry's largest stack tumbler: 55-pound stack tumbler that provides greater drying capacity and laundromat owners another tool to drive greater revenue. Scan-Pay-Wash: industry's first cashless payment technology solution that does not require an app download. Acquired Metropolitan Laundry Machinery Sales, a proven laundry equipment distributor serving customers across the greater New York area, expanding Alliance's direct presence in the attractive Northeast market. Launched Stax-X stacked washer dryer, the first product fully developed at Alliance's engineering facility in Thailand. Aligned with Alliance's local-for-local manufacturing strategy, Stax-X is designed for regional markets with its combined washer-extractor and tumble dryer that saves floor space and provides commercial-grade performance. POST-QUARTER HIGHLIGHTS Completed successful IPO on October 9, 2025, following which Alliance used net proceeds from the IPO and cash on-hand to repay $525.0 million of debt to deliver a 3.1x IPO adjusted net leverage ratio1. The Term Loan repricing combined with the repayment delivers an approximate $46.0 million annualized interest savings at current debt levels. Received a one notch credit rating upgrade from S&P Global to B+ (positive) and an outlook upgrade from Moody's Ratings to B2 (positive). 1 IPO adjusted net leverage ratio reflects September 30, 2025 Net debt to Adjusted EBITDA, adjusted for the debt repayment of $505.7 million related to IPO proceeds. CONFERENCE CALL INFORMATION Alliance will host a conference call to discuss this quarter's results at 8:00 am Eastern Time today, November 13, 2025. To listen to the conference call, a live audio webcast will be available on the Alliance's Investor Relations website at https://ir.alliancelaundry.com/news-events/ir-calendar . A replay of the webcast will be available after the call. To participate in the conference call, analysts and investors can dial 1 (800) 267-6316 and international participants can dial 1 (203) 518-9783. The Conference ID is ALH3Q25. Participants should dial in at least 10 minutes prior to the call. ABOUT ALLIANCE LAUNDRY Alliance Laundry makes the world cleaner as a provider of the highest quality commercial laundry systems. Our laundry solutions are available under five respected brands, sold and supported by a global network of select distributors. We serve approximately 150 countries with a team of more than 4,000 employees. Our brands include Speed Queen®, UniMac®, Huebsch®, Primus® and IPSO®. Together, they present a full line of commercial washing machines, dryers, and ironers (with load capacities from 20–400 lb. or 9–180 kg.) and support service. You can also enjoy the superior wash and fabric care of commercial-grade laundry equipment in your home through our legendary Speed Queen® washers and dryers. For more information, visit www.alliancelaundry.com . NON-GAAP FINANCIAL MEASURES We regularly review non-GAAP measures to evaluate our business, measure our performance and manage our operations, including identifying trends affecting our business, formulating business plans and making strategic decisions. We believe that non-GAAP measures provide an additional way of viewing aspects of our operations that, when viewed together with our GAAP results, provide a more complete understanding of our results of operations and the factors and trends affecting our business. These non-GAAP financial measures are also used by our management to evaluate financial results and to plan and forecast future periods. Non-GAAP financial measures should be considered a supplement to, and not a substitute for, or superior to, the corresponding measures calculated in accordance with GAAP. Non-GAAP financial measures used by us may differ from the non-GAAP measures used by other companies, including our competitors. "Adjusted EBITDA" represents Net income before provision for income taxes, interest expense, depreciation and amortization. Adjusted EBITDA is also adjusted for the discrete items that management excluded in analyzing the segments' operating performance, such as refinancing and debt related costs, share-based compensation, strategic transaction costs, foreign exchange on intercompany loans and other non-recurring items which management believes are not indicative of the Company's ongoing operating performance. "Adjusted EBITDA Margin" represents Adjusted EBITDA divided by Net revenues. Management utilizes Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA Margin as measures of operating performance. Management believes Adjusted EBITDA is a useful measure to help readers of our financial statements evaluate our operating performance and facilitates more meaningful comparisons with industry peers. Our calculation of non-GAAP measures may differ from similarly titled measures used by other companies, and therefore may not be directly comparable. In evaluating these metrics, investors should be aware that in the future we may incur expenses similar to those eliminated in this presentation. "Adjusted net income" represents Net income adjusted to exclude certain expenses not representative of our ongoing operations and other charges. These adjustments include, but are not limited to, refinancing and debt related costs, share-based compensation, strategic transaction costs, foreign exchange on intercompany loans and other non-recurring items. "Adjusted net income per share attributable to common stockholders – diluted" represents Adjusted net income divided by the weighted average number of diluted shares outstanding for the relevant period. "Net debt" represents our total debt less Cash and cash equivalents. "Net Debt to Adjusted EBITDA" represents total debt less Cash and cash equivalents divided by Adjusted EBITDA for the relevant period. "IPO adjusted net leverage" represents Net debt divided by Adjusted EBITDA giving effect to the repayment of debt with our IPO proceeds as if it had occurred at the ending of the relevant period. SEGMENT INFORMATION Our business is organized into two reportable segments, North America and International. The Company uses Segment net revenues, Segment Adjusted EBITDA and Segment Adjusted EBITDA Margin as its measures of performance. The Company allocates certain costs including manufacturing variances, customer support expenses and selling and general expenses which are incurred in our global operations to the reportable segments in determining Segment Adjusted EBITDA. We define "Segment Adjusted EBITDA" as, on a segment basis, net income excluding interest income/expense, income taxes, depreciation and amortization. Segment Adjusted EBITDA is also adjusted for the discrete items that management excluded in analyzing the segments' operating performance, such as refinancing and debt related costs, share-based compensation, strategic transaction costs, foreign exchange on intercompany loans and other non-recurring items which management believes are not indicative of the Company's ongoing operating performance. Segment Adjusted EBITDA is a measure of operating performance of our reportable segments and may not be comparable to similar measures reported by other companies. A telephone replay will be available one hour after the end of the conference until November 19, 2025, by dialing: US (Toll Free): +1-855-669-9658 International: +1-412-317-0088 Canada (Toll Free): +1-855-669-9658 Replay Passcode: 4694549 About UCLOUDLINK GROUP INC. UCLOUDLINK is the world’s first and leading mobile data traffic sharing marketplace, pioneering the sharing economy business model for the telecommunications industry. The Company’s products and services deliver unique value propositions to mobile data users, handset and smart-hardware companies, mobile virtual network operators (MVNOs) and mobile network operators (MNOs). Leveraging its innovative cloud SIM technology and architecture, the Company has redefined the mobile data connectivity experience by allowing users to gain access to mobile data traffic allowance shared by network operators on its marketplace, while providing reliable connectivity, high speeds and competitive pricing. title: Living the Winnebago legacy: How Mark Nevils is telling our story for a new generation
summary: The pioneering spirit has always been at the heart of Winnebago. From its first revolutionary campers nearly 70 years ago, to game-changing vehicles like the EKKO and Revel, and innovative technologies like Winnebago Connect that elevate the user experience in products such as the View/Navion, Winnebago’s legacy is rooted in innovation.
body_text: The pioneering spirit has always been at the heart of Winnebago. From its first revolutionary campers nearly 70 years ago, to game-changing vehicles like the EKKO and Revel, and innovative technologies like Winnebago ConnectTM that elevate the user experience in products such as the View/Navion, Winnebago’s legacy is rooted in innovation. Embodying that spirit means not only honoring Winnebago’s rich past but forging new roads to explore. Mark Nevils, senior manager of brand strategy and product marketing, is living that legacy every day, championing the products, stories and experiences that resonate far beyond the journey and stay with you long after the road ends. Nevils brings together the best of what he’s learned over two decades in brand storytelling, creative strategy and product marketing to help Winnebago find new ways to reach outdoor enthusiasts and bring its products to life. Fueling adventure through storytelling Nevils grew up in St. Louis, studied journalism and strategic communications at the University of Missouri and received his MBA from Drake University. Since then, he has been helping classic American companies like Maytag, Polaris, Indian Motorcycle and now Winnebago find compelling ways to showcase their products and make them come alive for customers. When you ask Nevils what motivates him in his role, he’ll tell you there are four driving forces at play: helping to serve and protect a classic American brand, working with the brand’s world-class marketing team, using storytelling to connect Winnebago’s products with people and the impact that Winnebago has on the people who enjoy its RVs. He is energized by the difference we can make on our customers and their families, and says adventure, family bonding, healing and discovery are at the heart of everything we do at Winnebago. A brand in motion Nevils explains that the Winnebago development team spends time camping with customers, learning their lifestyles and specific scenarios to gain insights they can apply to design. He and his team receive the culmination of product development and engineering, then help author the story. “I love watching our team play part psychologist, part strategist—people at Winnebago have a knack for truly understanding our customers’ needs, desires and even their unspoken dreams,” Nevils says. “Our goal is to apply this deep empathy to build bridges between our products and our customers, ensuring that every message isn't just heard but felt in a meaningful way.” A job like that needs a team up for the challenge, and Nevils is inspired by his colleagues every day, some of whom enjoy a long history with the brand. “It’s fascinating to walk the halls in Forest City and see people who have worked at Winnebago for decades and even multiple generations before and after them,” he says. “It’s another poignant reason our team is so committed to protecting this special place and our collective future.” Winnebago is embracing a period of self-reflection, transformation and resurgence as it builds on its heritage as an American icon and launches the next generation of game-changing RVs, like the Sunflyer, 2026 RV News Class C RV of the Year. “Our humble mandate is to secure the next 67 years by building on the grit, ingenuity and hardworking Midwestern DNA that got us here in the first place,” Nevils says. “We are committed to listening more, serving with passion, innovating thoughtfully and delivering affordable, high-quality products faster than ever.” For Nevils, heritage and innovation are inseparable: “We like to say we ‘live the legacy’ in everything we do, meaning it’s not just a reverent nod to the past, but a daily commitment to embrace that same pioneering spirit with every task we take on, big or small.” Meeting the moment Nevils knows well that consumer expectations for RVs are evolving just like they do for the cars we drive and the technology we carry in our pockets. “We plan to engage a new generation of customers with the power of our brand, then delight them with our own standard of product quality and innovation, proving why we believe when you buy from us it’s not just an RV – it’s a Winnebago,” he says. “We’re so much more than an RV company – with our family culture and the most vibrant owner community on the planet, you’re instantly part of something bigger. It’s a story that Nevils believes has a place for everyone. “We want our brand and community to be welcoming to people of all cultures, ethnicities and walks of life,” he says. “We believe time spent outdoors is priceless and the life experiences waiting to be discovered should be for everyone.”

title: What Your Health Journey Looks Like With Loop
summary: Navigate healthcare with 24/7 medical guidance, faster claims, and support when you need it most. Loop makes your health journey less stressful.
body_text: Most of us don't think about healthcare until something goes wrong. A fever that won't break. A nagging pain that keeps you up at night. A late-night worry that something might be seriously wrong. And suddenly, you're not just dealing with feeling unwell—you're trying to figure out a complex system. Which doctor should I see, and how do I know they're the right one? Where should I get these tests done? How does my insurance work? The questions pile up exactly when you have the least energy to answer them. Here's something we've learned from talking to thousands of people navigating the Indian healthcare system: it asks a lot of you exactly when you're least equipped to give it. The sicker you feel, the more decisions you need to make, often without clear information or support. At Loop, we believe your health journey should work differently—the more you need help, the more support you should have. Your health journey is every touchpoint you have with healthcare—from noticing the first symptom to getting a diagnosis, receiving treatment, and returning to wellness. It includes the doctors you see, the tests you take, the questions you ask, the claims you file, and the preventive care that keeps you healthy between illnesses. {{divider}} Why Healthcare Often Feels So Complicated When you're unwell, you start by trying to understand what's wrong. For many of us, that means searching online, reading through symptoms, trying to figure out if what we're experiencing is something to worry about or if it will pass on its own. It's not always easy to know. Then comes finding the right doctor. You might get recommendations from friends or family, search online, or call a few clinics. But it's often unclear which specialist you need, who's accepting new patients, or how to compare your options in a meaningful way. Getting diagnostics done becomes its own project—different labs have different prices for the same tests, and the reports come back filled with medical terminology. You're left wondering what the numbers mean and what you should do next. Medical expenses add up quickly. Even with insurance, many everyday health costs—medicines, supplements, preventive care—come from your own pocket first. And then there's navigating insurance claims: understanding what's covered, gathering the right documentation, submitting forms, and waiting for updates. For many people, this process feels uncertain and time-consuming. Through all of this, you're managing everything yourself, often while not feeling well. It takes genuine effort and energy that you'd rather spend on getting better. Loop was created to change this experience. {{divider}} The Loop Way: Healthcare With Real Guidance Loop brings your healthcare experience into one connected place, with human support at every step. Not just tools and information, but guidance from people who know healthcare and want to help you navigate it. Think of it as having someone knowledgeable by your side throughout your health journey—someone who can answer your questions, help you make decisions, and handle the complexity so you can focus on feeling better. When Something Feels Off, Help Is Already There There's often a moment when something doesn't feel quite right, but you're not sure what to do about it. Maybe it warrants attention, maybe it doesn't. That uncertainty itself can be stressful. With Loop, you have 24x7 access to medical advisors —healthcare professionals who respond in under 60 seconds. You can reach out whenever you need to, day or night. Here's how this works in practice: You notice a symptom that concerns you. Instead of wondering whether you should wait, search online, or head to a doctor immediately, you can message your medical advisor through the Loop app. Within a minute, they're talking with you, understanding your situation, and helping you figure out the best next step. Do you need to see a doctor right away? Would it help to monitor your symptoms for a day or two? Are there simple measures you can take at home? You get clear, professional guidance based on your specific situation. This approach helps in several ways—you address health concerns earlier, when they're often easier to manage, while avoiding unnecessary worry about things that aren't serious. Most importantly, you have clarity about what to do next, which brings peace of mind when you need it most. {{divider}} Finding the Right Specialist for Your Needs When you do need to see a doctor, finding the right one matters. But it's not always straightforward to know which type of specialist is best for your symptoms, or how to identify doctors with the right experience. Your Loop medical advisor helps with this. They work with you to understand what you're experiencing, then help match you with the right specialist from a network of 50+ doctors across 12+ medical fields. These are doctors Loop has vetted for quality and expertise. Sometimes the right specialty isn't obvious. That persistent cough—does it need a pulmonologist, an allergist, or an ENT specialist? Your advisor helps you think through these questions and make an informed choice. You can book consultations directly through the Loop app. This guided approach means you're more likely to see the right doctor the first time, which often leads to better care and less time spent navigating the system. {{divider}} Making Diagnostics Simpler If you need lab tests, there are often several questions: Which lab should I use? What will it cost? When will I get results? What will those results mean? Loop streamlines this process. You can book from trusted labs through the app. Many tests offer home sample collection, so a trained professional comes to you at a time that works for your schedule. Reports are delivered to both WhatsApp and email, usually within the timeframe the lab specifies. What happens next is particularly valuable: your medical advisor helps you understand what the results mean . They can explain the numbers, answer your questions, and talk through any next steps with you. This removes a lot of the stress and confusion that often comes with medical testing. You're not left alone trying to interpret complex medical information. {{divider}} Access to Wellness Essentials You Use Many of the things that help us stay healthy day-to-day—medicines, supplements, dental care, fitness programs, mental health support—aren't typically covered by traditional insurance, even though they're important for overall wellness. Loop provides access to these healthcare essentials through partnerships with trusted providers—medicines through 1MG and Apollo, nutrition and supplements, dental and elderly care, fitness through Cult.fit, even pet care (because the health of family members, including furry ones, affects household wellbeing). Having these resources in one place, often at better prices, makes it easier to prioritize your health in practical, everyday ways. {{divider}} Support That Helps You Stay Well The healthcare we need before we get sick matters just as much as the care we receive afterward. But preventive wellness can be hard to fit into busy lives, especially when programs feel generic or disconnected from reality. Loop's Wellness program is designed to fit into daily life—stress management sessions that offer practical techniques you can use, nutrition guidance based on what you eat and realistic changes you might want to make, mental wellbeing support for when work or life pressures start affecting how you feel physically, and preventive health check-ups that helps you understand your health and catch potential issues early. These aren't dramatic transformations, but meaningful improvements that compound over time. That's what good preventive care looks like. {{divider}} Claims That Work the Way They Should Insurance claims are challenging to navigate for most people. Traditional claims processes often involve several pain points: unclear requirements, multiple document submissions, long waits with little visibility into what's happening, and sometimes rejections that require starting over. Many people have spent weeks or months getting claims processed. Loop's in-app claims feature addresses these challenges directly with a step-by-step guided process that shows you exactly which documents you need. The app provides a clear checklist, so you know what's required before you begin. You upload everything directly in the app—discharge summaries, bills, prescriptions, all in one organized place. No need to email different departments or keep track of multiple submission channels. Real-time status tracking shows you exactly where your claim stands, and you can check anytime without needing to call and ask. If something's missing or needs clarification, claims specialists reach out promptly with specific guidance. They tell you exactly what's needed and help you provide it. Faster processing happens naturally when the system is designed well. That's meaningful time saved (often the difference between a week and three weeks) and money back in your account sooner. This is insurance working as it should: clear, transparent, and helpful when you need it. {{divider}} Healthcare That Puts Your Experience First Most healthcare platforms provide information and tools, then leave you to navigate the rest on your own. They're helpful to a point, but they don't fundamentally change the experience of managing your health. Loop works differently by guiding your entire journey. A medical advisor is available 24/7 when you have questions or concerns. You get help finding the right specialist for your specific situation, diagnostics that come with explanation and context, access to wellness resources that fit into daily life, preventive support that helps you stay healthier, and a claims process designed to work with you, not against you. The result is a health journey that feels supported, connected, and manageable—even during difficult times. {{divider}} You're Not Alone in This Health challenges are deeply personal, but they don't have to be lonely. You shouldn't have to figure out complex medical decisions while worried or in pain. You shouldn't have to navigate insurance bureaucracy while recovering from illness. You shouldn't have to research specialists or interpret test results entirely on your own. With Loop, you have genuine partnership through your health journey. Medical advisors help you understand what's happening when symptoms appear. The right doctors are identified for your specific needs when you need care. Diagnostics are explained in clear language when tests are needed. Preventive support is there consistently when staying healthy matters. And when claims arise, the process works. This represents a different philosophy about what healthcare should be. One that recognizes you're dealing with complex situations that affect your life, your family, and your peace of mind. One that provides concrete support instead of just information. One that understands guidance matters, especially during uncertain times. Your health journey matters—every concern that keeps you up at night, every decision you're trying to make, every moment you've felt lost in the medical system. All of it matters. Loop is here to make that journey clearer, more supported, and less stressful. Not perfect—because healthcare is complex and every situation is unique—but genuinely better in ways that make a tangible difference in your life. From the first symptom to full recovery, you have support. You have guidance. You have someone in your corner.

title: The Magnum Ice Cream Company successfully completes €3 billion debut bond issuance
summary: The Magnum Ice Cream Company (TMICC), the world’s largest ice cream company, today announced the successful completion of a €3 billion debut bond issuance by Magnum ICC Finance B.V., across four tranches.Commenting on the successful issuance, Abhijit Bhattacharya, CFO, The Magnum Ice Cream Company noted “Issuing our inaugural public bond i...
body_text: The Magnum Ice Cream Company (TMICC), the world’s largest ice cream company, today announced the successful completion of a €3 billion debut bond issuance by Magnum ICC Finance B.V., across four tranches. Commenting on the successful issuance, Abhijit Bhattacharya, CFO, The Magnum Ice Cream Company noted “Issuing our inaugural public bond is an important milestone for The Magnum Ice Cream Company as we embark on our journey as a standalone ice cream company. The level of interest shown by the market was fantastic, with the order book being oversubscribed by over seven times. This clearly indicates that our strategy and story as the world’s leading ice cream company resonates with investors.” The debut issuance was completed under the newly established €8 billion Euro Medium Term Note programme of Magnum ICC Finance B.V. guaranteed by The Magnum Ice Cream Company B.V. and The Magnum Ice Cream Company HoldCo Netherlands B.V. (the “EMTN Programme”). The issuance comprises (i) €750 million 2.750 per cent. fixed rate senior unsecured notes due February 2029; (ii) €750 million 3.250 per cent. fixed rate senior unsecured notes due November 2031; (iii) €750 million 3.750 per cent. fixed rate senior unsecured notes due November 2034; and (iv) €750 million 4.000 per cent. fixed rate senior unsecured notes due November 2037 (together, the “Notes”). The net proceeds of the issue of the Notes will be used for the general corporate purposes of the TMICC Group including to facilitate the demerger of the TMICC Group from the Unilever Group. The Notes have been rated “BBB” by S&P and “Baa2” by Moody’s and application has been made to the London Stock Exchange for the Notes to be admitted to trading on the London Stock Exchange’s International Securities Market with effect on or around 26th November 2025. Pricing Supplements in connection with the Notes dated 24th November 2025 and the Base Admission Particulars dated 13th November 2025 in connection with the EMTN Programme are available on the IR section of the company website .

title: Industry Expert Shares Insights for Independent Dealers Nationwide
summary: America’s Car-Mart’s Doug Turner to Discuss Inventory Management at NIADA 2025 Conference
body_text: In the used car business, few things matter more than having the right inventory—cars, trucks, and SUVs— at the right time, in the right condition. Inventory impacts everything, from customer experience to operational efficiency to the bottom line. Getting it right isn’t easy, but for leaders like Doug Turner , it’s a challenge built on decades of experience and constant improvement. As Senior Director of Remarketing at America’s Car-Mart, Doug helps our teams make smarter, faster, more informed decisions about the vehicles we buy and how we prepare them for customers. “Buying and reconditioning is where it all starts,” he says. “If the car’s in great shape, our customers have a much better chance at success.” Doug brings his expertise to the national stage again this year, presenting at the 2025 National Independent Automobile Dealers Association (NIADA) Conference and sharing strategies that help independent dealers nationwide improve their inventory performance. At Car-Mart, we believe in sharing what we’ve learned to help others succeed. Whether it’s through leadership, innovation, or industry collaboration, we’re committed to supporting independent dealers and the communities they serve. Sharing Insights That Help Dealers – and Communities – Thrive Doug’s presentation, “The Heart of the Matter – Inventory Management,” offers practical insights to help dealers better serve theircustomers. He’ll take a deep dive into best practices for sourcing and reconditioning vehicles. He’ll also cover inventory management across single-point and multi-location dealerships, with a focus on maximizing efficiency from purchase to sale. He’ll demonstrate how smarter buying decisions and more efficient reconditioning result in better outcomes for both dealers and their customers. Doug’s topics include: · Data-driven vehicle sourcing – using data to drive your decisions, not your gut, to buy the right car, at the right time, for the right customers. · Reducing cycle times – removing one to two days from each step of the inventory process: buying, transporting, reconditioning, and retail-ready preparation. · Reconditioning for success – why the condition of the vehicle is directly tied to customer satisfaction and success. · Understanding customer needs vs. wants – stocking vehicles that align with what customers truly need. · Using AI and technology in auctions – how digital tools and AI-enhanced inspections are creating more objective, consistent vehicle descriptions, and smarter buying decisions. Doug will be joined by a representative from the National Auto Auction Association (NAAA), who will discuss the changes being implemented at the auctions, especially how AI is transforming auction dynamics. About Doug Turner – A Career Built on Experience—and Purpose Doug’s automotive journey began in high school, washing cars at a dealership in Marion, Ind. After earning a degree in business management (marketing/sales promotions) from Ball State University, Muncie, Ind., in 1992, he worked in tire sales and management at a Sears Auto Center. He then moved into leadership roles in operations, purchasing, and remarketing at J.D. Byrider, where he spent 24 years. He also worked at America’s Auto Auction for a year before joining America’s Car-Mart in 2024. Doug and Car-Mart associate discussing project plans. Doug was drawn to Car-Mart because of its strong culture, community focus, and the leadership of CEO Doug Campbell. “I had heard a lot about the company and its great employee culture. I love this business. I love the buy here pay here business model,” he says, Reflecting on his first days at Car-Mart, Doug recalls, “The welcome I received and the support during my move were tremendous. I knew right away that Car-Mart was the right fit.” Doug is passionate about Car-Mart’s mission to provide reliable, affordable vehicles to people who may not have access elsewhere. “We’re not just selling cars, we’re helping people get to work, the grocery store, and school,” says Doug. “We’re helping customers live their lives.” He also serves as Chairperson of the Board for the ARA (Automotive Remarketing Alliance), after a two-year term as president. He has volunteered with this organization since 2000. “It’s good and healthy to be part of these automotive organizations—they raise visibility, bring great people together, and create opportunities to give back,” Doug concludes. “It’s a meaningful way to support and strengthen the industry.” Ready to Drive Your Career Forward? At America’s Car-Mart, we’re more than a dealership—we’re a team of people passionate about helping customers and communities thrive. If you’re looking for a place where your ideas matter and your work makes a real difference, join us. Explore current opportunities across our 12-state network and start your journey with Car-Mart today at Car-Mart.com/careers .

AEO vs SEO: Key Differences Explained
summary: Understand the differences between AEO and SEO. Learn when to use answer engine optimization vs traditional SEO to maximize your AI search visibility.
body_text: If you’ve worked in search engine optimization long enough, you’ve probably gotten used to a rhythm: keyword research, technical tweaks, backlinks, rinse and repeat. But something’s shifting. Instead of “Googling” everything, people are asking AI assistants , chatbots , and voice interfaces for answers. And those systems aren’t scanning web pages the same way humans, or even traditional search crawlers do. That’s where AEO (Answer Engine Optimization) comes in. It’s the emerging discipline of optimizing your brand, products, and content to be understood and surfaced by AI-powered engines . So, what’s really different between AEO and SEO? And how do you prepare for a world where “position 1” doesn’t mean what it used to? Let’s dig in. What Is SEO (Search Engine Optimization)? We’ll start with familiar ground. SEO is the process of improving your website’s visibility in search engines like Google and Bing. That typically means: Targeting high-intent keywords Building topical authority with relevant content Optimizing metadata, headings, and structure for crawlability Earning backlinks and improving domain authority Enhancing UX signals: page speed, mobile responsiveness, engagement In short: SEO helps humans find you through search results. But traditional SEO was built for a web where users clicked links , and where search engines indexed static pages . That world’s changing fast. What Is AEO (Answer Engine Optimization)? AEO flips the perspective. Instead of optimizing for clicks, you’re optimizing for answers. AI-driven engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and Bing Copilot don’t send users to a list of links, they generate answers directly, often citing sources inline. That means the game is more about providing answers that get referenced, instead of showing up high on the SERPs . AEO focuses on: Structuring information so AI systems can understand and reuse it Using semantic markup and knowledge graphs to define entities and relationships Ensuring your brand data, products, and content are machine-readable Feeding large language models (LLMs) and retrieval systems with context-rich, factually consistent data Think of it as SEO’s evolved cousin; the one fluent in both natural language and data science. AEO vs SEO: The Key Differences Aspect SEO AEO Goal Rank high in search results Be selected, cited, or referenced by AI answer engines Platform Web browsers Conversational AI platforms Optimization Focus Keywords, backlinks, page experience Entities, relationships, structured data Measurement Click-through rate, impressions, rankings Mentions, citations, inclusion in AI responses Tools & Techniques Google Search Console, Ahrefs, on-page optimization, backlink building Knowledge graph alignment, structured schema, AEO tools like Bear AI Content Style Keyword-focused and scannable Semantically rich, contextually precise, machine-legible Traditional SEO is about visibility in a ranked list. AEO is about trust (built via citations) and interpretability (clear answers and well-structured content) in an AI’s knowledge model. Why AEO Matters (and Why It’s Taking Off Now) The shift from SEO to AEO isn’t theoretical, it’s already happening. Over 70 percent of adults in the US report using ChatGPT as a search engine. In 2025 and beyond, brands that optimize for AI will gain an edge. It’s a fast moving discipline where first-mover advantage is rewarded. AI-powered search and conversational assistants are rapidly becoming the new interface for discovery: ChatGPT and Perplexity deliver direct answers, not ten blue links Google Search Generative Experience (SGE) summarizes SERP results in one AI-generated paragraph Voice assistants like Alexa and Siri increasingly rely on structured data, not raw HTML As a result, being “ranked #1” no longer guarantees visibility. If your brand isn’t part of the data layer these systems draw from, you’re invisible to AI-driven discovery, even if your SEO is perfect. That’s where AEO becomes crucial. It’s how you ensure your company’s information can be found, understood, and accurately represented by answer engines. How AEO and SEO Work Together To be clear. AEO isn’t replacing SEO. SEO is still hugely valuable for brands looking to tap into high-intent traffic. Rather, it’s expanding it. You still need the fundamentals: fast pages, valuable content, strong backlinks. Those signals feed credibility into any model, human or AI. But to truly future-proof your search presence, you need to bridge both worlds. Here’s how they complement each other: Technical SEO provides structure which supports AEO schema and entity markup Content optimization ensures clarity which improves AI interpretability Authority building earns backlinks which become trust signals for AI models sourcing answers AEO in Practice: How AI Engines “Think” When an AI assistant answers a question like “best cybersecurity platform for startups,” it’s not just retrieving web pages. It’s building a semantic map of entities, companies, products, features, and connecting them to concepts like “endpoint protection” or “SOC 2 compliance.” If your company isn’t represented in that knowledge graph with accurate, accessible, and machine-readable data, you’re out of the conversation. AEO ensures you’re in it. That means: Defining your brand, product, and use cases in structured formats (schema.org, JSON-LD) Feeding verified data into public and private knowledge bases Maintaining consistency across your site, press mentions, and product listings This isn’t the kind of optimization you do once and forget. It’s ongoing training, just like AI itself. Where Bear AI Fits In Most search visibility tools were built for the classic SEO approach: keywords, rankings, backlinks. Bear AI is built for how people search today. It’s the first platform purpose-built for AEO and GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) . Giving you AI search visibility where traditional SEO tools can’t reach. Bear helps companies: Discover how and where their brand appears in AI-generated results across major answer engines Identify why certain competitors get cited instead of you Generate structured, machine-readable data that LLMs and answer engines actually consume Continuously monitor and optimize entity visibility across evolving AI ecosystems In short: Bear AI helps your brand show up where people no longer “search”, they ask. Whether you’re a B2B SaaS platform, cybersecurity startup, or consumer tech brand, Bear helps ensure your company is part of the answers that users see first. The Future: From Search Results to Search Relationships The shift from SEO to AEO is both a technical and philosophical shift. AI answer engines reward truth, context, and semantic clarity. Clever keyword placement and SEO hacks no longer cut it. That means your digital strategy needs to speak the language of both humans and machines. Bear AI exists to make that possible, helping your brand bridge the gap between traditional search visibility and generative discovery. Ready to Go Beyond SEO? With the direction search is moving, your marketing team needs to move beyond tracking just rankings and clicks. AEO is the next stage of visibility in an AI-driven web. Bear AI helps you understand how your brand appears in answer engines, and how to make sure you’re part of the conversation that’s shaping your category. Ready to start showing up more in AI search? Get started with Bear AI today . FAQ: AEO vs SEO 1. What is the main difference between AEO and SEO? SEO (Search Engine Optimization) focuses on improving your visibility in search engine results like Google or Bing. AEO (Answer Engine Optimization) focuses on helping AI search products like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini understand and reference your content when generating answers. 2. Do I still need SEO if I’m doing AEO? Yes, absolutely. SEO is still foundational. You’ll still need fast, well-structured pages, strong content, and backlinks. AEO builds on those principles by ensuring that your content is machine-readable and contextually clear enough for AI models to reference accurately. 3. How do I optimize for AEO? To optimize for AEO, focus on: Structured data: Use schema.org or JSON-LD markup to define entities. Clarity and consistency: Write content that clearly explains what your product, service, or topic is and how it relates to others. Fact-rich content: AI models value concise, verifiable information. Knowledge graph presence: Ensure your brand is represented across trusted databases and publications. Tools like Bear AI help by monitoring how and where your brand appears in AI-generated results, so you can see what’s working and where you’re being overlooked. 4. How is AEO measured? Unlike SEO, AEO isn’t about rankings or clicks. It’s about citations, mentions, and inclusion in AI-generated answers . AEO tools track how often and where your brand appears in responses from systems like Perplexity or ChatGPT, as well as how those mentions change over time. 5. Why is AEO becoming important now? AI-powered assistants are quickly replacing traditional search as the discovery layer of the web. Instead of “Googling,” people are simply asking questions—and trusting AI-generated summaries. If your brand’s data isn’t part of what these models draw from, you’re effectively invisible. 6. What kind of brands should focus on AEO? Any brand that publishes content online can benefit, but it’s especially relevant for: B2B SaaS and cybersecurity companies competing on thought leadership Consumer tech brands relying on credibility and product comparisons Startups wanting to appear authoritative in new AI-driven discovery channels If your audience is asking AI questions about your category, AEO should already be on your radar.

title: Enabling Targets for Structure-Based Drug Discovery
summary: Scientists rely on experimental and computational techniques to reveal, refine, and validate molecular structures, ensuring targets are ready for structure-based modeling and enabling the translation of molecular insight into new medicines.
body_text: Education Enabling Targets for Structure-Based Drug Discovery BY Schrödinger Editorial Team Nov 17, 2025 This is the second in a three-part series highlighting essential computational chemistry topics covered in the newly released Schrödinger Online Course bundle . Read on for a review of the various methods for obtaining and refining structures to enable structure-based drug discovery. The field of structure-based drug discovery (SBDD) took shape in the 1980s, when advances in X-ray crystallography first allowed scientists to visualize the three-dimensional shapes of biologically important proteins in atomic detail. For the first time, researchers could see exactly how drug molecules fit into their targets, like keys in molecular locks, and use that knowledge to guide the design of new therapeutics. These breakthroughs gave rise to powerful computational techniques such as molecular docking, which predicts how small molecules bind to proteins, and free energy perturbation (FEP), which can estimate binding strength with remarkable precision. Today, scientists use a range of powerful methods to reveal and refine molecular structures, from X-ray crystallography and cryo-electron microscopy to machine learning-based prediction tools. Computational modeling plays a central role in improving these structures and ensuring they accurately capture how proteins move and interact with potential drugs. Understanding these techniques, and knowing how to validate that a target is ready for structure-based modeling, is essential for translating molecular insight into new medicines. Methods for structure determination or prediction Experimental structure determination X-ray crystallography remains the primary source of structures in the Protein Data Bank and is one of the most established techniques for determining protein structures. Although an X-ray crystal structure can frequently be near-atomic resolution, this process requires significant time and resources, and flexible targets cannot be easily crystallized. Over the last decade, driven by advances in imaging technology and simplified sample preparation protocols, cryo-EM has emerged as a popular alternative method for protein structure determination at atomic resolution. Cryo-EM structures have an advantage over X-ray crystal structures in that structures can remain in their native states, including membrane-bound states, which is key for enabling G protein–coupled receptor (GPCR) and ion channel targets. Cryo-EM structures are, however, frequently lower resolution and in need of additional refinement to generate a high-confidence atomistic model of the system. Template-based structure prediction Methods like template-based homology modeling combine knowledge of template structures, utilizing all structural data where the target and query sequences match, with backbone data, which refers to the continuous sequence of atoms that forms a protein’s structural framework. Template-based homology modeling also leverages physics-based prediction methods for anything not explicitly captured in the template. While these models can be valuable, they also have limitations — they are generally more accurate the higher the sequence identity between the query and template sequence. Machine learning structure prediction Many in the world of drug discovery were introduced to machine learning structure prediction by the “AlphaFold moment” in the 2018 Critical Assessment of Structure Prediction (CASP) competition. In this breakthrough event, DeepMind’s AlphaFold dramatically outperformed all other protein structure prediction methods, signaling a turning point in structural biology. Since then, several generations of both general and specialized structure prediction models have been released, including AlphaFold2/3, Chai1/2, Boltz1/2, and RoseTTAFold-all-atom. Co-folding methods in particular have shown great promise However, the quality of the generated poses can be limited by how similar the target protein is to the structures included in the method’s training set. Despite their limitations, these models have the potential to vastly expand the number of targets that can be drugged through structure-based drug design methods. Structure assessment The output from any of the methods described above is a three-dimensional structure. An important next step for anyone working with one of these structures would be to evaluate the relevance and quality of the structure. Does it capture the biologically relevant conformation? Does it have a well-resolved ligand with a binding mode similar to what we’d expect for our project’s chemistry? Answering these questions can help differentiate between “a” structure and “the right” structure. Structure refinement Structures obtained from any of these methods are rarely, if ever, ready for immediate use in modeling or drug design without additional refinement and validation. Preparation and refinement methods, such as with Schrödinger’s Protein Preparation Workflow , and IFD-MD , can help fill in missing side chains or refine ligand placement in the binding site. These tools can help fix glaring mistakes and refine models, and are also fundamentally hypothesis generators that allow researchers to generate several models that could be profiled by FEP+ , Schrödinger’s industry-leading free energy perturbation technology. Enablement through rigorous validation The final step of structure enablement is to evaluate the predictive power of your structural model. This is done by using a computational assay, such as FEP+, and a series of known binders with experimental binding affinity to test how well the predicted affinities correlate to the experimental values. Poor correlation indicates that the structural model doesn’t sufficiently capture the biological system, suggesting that it would have limited utility for affinity prediction and other structure-based tasks. Strong correlations are the ultimate validation of structure quality and utility.
